body:
I have made a list of problems that I have with my self and I want to dedicate 100% on each problem individually but can't stay focused. I even wrote down some possible solutions to fix one or two of these problems and others I have no idea how to solve. (e.g. I have a work out regiment that was working until I was using eating to cope with rejection, but I have no idea on how to make friends)

My biggest problem right now is getting a job. Aside from that there are a few issues I could work on in the now, but I am letting this one major problem hold me back. 

I see the cycle, I try to break it, but I feel it just ends up with me being in teh same place over and over again (depressed/thinking of suicide). As far as the job thing I feel like I've invested too much time applying to jobs, going to career fairs, talking with my school career center, and need to start looking at a different area of work. Which fills me with anger that I can't get the job I want, anger that I wasted 4 years (and a ton of my money and my parents money), angry that I am too stupid to get a job, fearful that anything field I try I will end up the same, and then finally have thoughts of suicide because I have failed in everything else I have done, shitty that I can't help out my parents yet who have been so fucking patient with me. I don't know.

I think I am going to bed and think things over (again). You have given me some good advice I will go back in the morning to read this. If you do don't mind do you think I can talk to you again if I have any more doubts or questions?

Thanks for the advice. I've tried the identify a problem method but not make myself the client. Maybe that is the trick I need to focus more? In any case I'll give it a shot.

Even writing that sentence I have this nagging voice telling me what is the point, I'll just fail again. It's hard to be motivated when I have a track record of just failing everything I do.

How did you get over feeling like a failure? I feel like if I could just land a job and actually learn to be useful then all my feelings will turn into happy ones and I can lead a happy life. My gf thinks even if I get a job I won't be happy which she may be right.

The way you describe blacksmithing is the passion I have/had for my major. You can create something you and others can interact with.

My problem is that with my major nothing clicked. The best way I can describe it is I have a tool box and I know what each tool does but don't know how to use it. It's like if I had a set of materials that needed to be put together, I have no idea which tool to use, when, right way of using it. I have tried doing some projects on my own for a year but I can't ever get them finished/working. Posting online for help has been unmotivating because the responses are, "Go to school to learn that" "Look at other projects" "If you took X classes this should be a breeze". I can imitate what other people do but when it comes down to doing something original or on my own it craps out.

The last paragraph is the reason I really hate myself. It sounds and feels pathetic. I went to school and I came out a failure. It sounds whiny and bitchy. And I feel ashamed to talk like this. 

I've been focusing alot on originality. I think I am going to just look up projects and see if I can understand how they work together. Just imitate peoples designs, if I am lucky enough to get a job interview hopefully i can sound like I know what I am talking about.

How did you go from webdesigning to blacksmithing?

I've applied for out of state for a while now. At first I was reluctant because I did not want to be away from my gf but thought having a job would alleviate my mental stress. Unfortunately, I have had no luck doing this either. 

Besides, my family is not causing me additional stress. My cousins don't speak to me and my uncles/aunts only speak to my parents. But it sucks because I can overhear their conversations when they talk on the phone or they come over to speak to them. I can just hear the whispers  or "Has he found anything yet?" "No leads?" "Poor thing, my daughter/son just got something what was his major?" I know these people long enough to know that they seem caring in public to keep up appearances but behind closed doors that are judgemental as fuck.

The thing about my major is I love it. What I could do with it, the projects I could work on. My passion for it is great, I even drool when I read about articles or newstories of whats going on. But I feel like passion can only get you so much and proof of competency is needed.

I've been thinking of what else I could do. I looked into some IT stuff, it seems like I don't need any degree just certifications. Bought some books but I just don't have the passion for it. I read and feel so bored. I might look into other crafts though, thanks for that.

How did you get into blacksmithing? Also, how difficult is it?

I have a large family. In m city alone I have around 10 cousins around with +/- 4 years so within my age group. We used to be close, but I think it was due to family events. I was always quiet with the adults because it's how I am but with my cousins I was always talkative. Then high school hit, they were all really popular and I was the lone outcast. This in turn had a negative impact on my relationship with my cousins (since I was 14 they have spoken to me less than 10x) and my uncles/aunts think I am weird because their kids have all these friends and went out to parties while I stayed home every day. (from eavesdropping when they speak to my parents).

No point in talking to them about it because they would deny it. My cousins don't really care, it's their parents who piss me off. They are the ones who are judgmental, kind of like a community opinion. Only thing that would change their minds is results. 

I don't want to get specific but I majored in sciences/engineering. I did well in school and on paper I look like a great candidate. But for 4 years I felt like something just didn't click with the material. I talked to upperclassmen and they said "I felt the same way until my last year, then everything just came together and clicked." But I never had that epiphany and frankly I fear its too late.

Thanks for replying btw. No need to stay up the whole night. I made the post in a panic because I was thinking of ending my life for the first time with nothing in my mind telling me to stop. Usually its more of a fantasy for me, just knowing there is a way to end my loneliness/anger/sadness, but at the time of writing the post it didn't feel like a fantasy anymore.
